description: The image presents two side-by-side bar charts illustrating the relationship between Fleiss Kappa (a measure of inter-rater reliability) and two different ambiguity metrics—“Ambiguity Std” on the left and “Max Ambiguity” on the right—likely in the context of evaluating human or model responses to social engineering prompts in the era of large language models (LLMs). Both charts share the same vertical axis, labeled “Fleiss Kappa,” ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. In the left chart, the horizontal axis is labeled “Ambiguity Std” and displays four categories: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94. The corresponding Fleiss Kappa values are 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24, respectively, with bars decreasing in height from left to right except for a slight rise at the last point. In the right chart, the horizontal axis is labeled “Max Ambiguity” and displays three integer categories: 1, 2, and 3. The corresponding Fleiss Kappa values are 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, respectively, with a clear decreasing trend. All bars are colored in shades of blue, with darker tones for higher values. The charts suggest that as ambiguity increases (whether measured by standard deviation or maximum value), agreement among raters (Fleiss Kappa) tends to decrease, indicating greater difficulty in consistently evaluating ambiguous social engineering content.
